prompt: `first/main.go` called `slog.Debug("not shown")` and nothing appeared. Why?
hint: What level does the default logger record from?

choices.text: Debug records go to standard error
choices.why: The capture showed both outputs together; nothing was written anywhere.

choices.text: The default logger records `INFO` and above
choices.why: Right. The options of the next program lowered the level to `DEBUG`.

choices.text: `slog.Debug` needs a context argument
choices.why: `DebugContext` is the variant with one; `Debug` works without.

choices.text: A message with a space in it is dropped
choices.why: `order placed` has a space and was logged.

prompt: What does a `JSONHandler` record keep that a sentence written with `fmt.Printf` loses?

choices.text: The colours of the terminal
choices.why: Neither has colour; the difference is structure.

choices.text: Typed, named values
choices.why: Right. A number stays a number that a log search can sum or filter.

choices.text: The exact time down to the nanosecond
choices.why: Time is an attribute of both, and this lesson removed it on purpose.

choices.text: The name of the function that logged
choices.why: That needs `AddSource`, for either handler.

prompt: A team moves a program from `TextHandler` to `JSONHandler`. What has to change in the calls that write the records?

choices.text: Every call's arguments, to JSON strings
choices.why: The handler encodes; the calls pass plain values.

choices.text: Every call, from `Info` to `InfoJSON`
choices.why: There is no such method.

choices.text: Nothing; only where the logger is made
choices.why: Right. `handlers/main.go` wrote the same calls through both.

choices.text: The levels, since JSON has no `WARN`
choices.why: JSON records carry the level as a string like any other.

prompt: The option that removes or rewrites an attribute before it is written, used here to drop the time, is `ReplaceAttr` in `slog.___Options`.
hint: The struct passed to both handlers.

choices.text: Nothing; it adds the attributes to `log`
choices.why: `log` is unchanged. `With` returns a new logger, `req` in the program.

choices.text: A new logger that adds them to every record
choices.why: Right. Every line from `req` began with `request_id` and `user`.

choices.text: A record, ready to be written
choices.why: Records are made by the logging calls, not by `With`.

choices.text: A group called `request_id`
choices.why: Groups come from `slog.Group` or `WithGroup`.

prompt: `req.Info("odd number of arguments", "order")` wrote `"!BADKEY":"order"`. Why did `slog` write the record at all instead of failing?
hint: What would a failed logging call hide?

choices.text: Because `!BADKEY` is a valid key a program may choose
choices.why: It is the marker `slog` uses for a value with no key, not a choice.

choices.text: It panicked and recovered
choices.why: No panic happened; the record was written normally.

choices.text: A failing log call would hide the line someone needs
choices.why: Right, and `go vet` catches the mistake before the program runs.

choices.text: Logging calls cannot return errors
choices.why: They are designed not to, for the reason in the right answer; nothing stopped the designers otherwise.

prompt: A payment library logs a struct that holds a card number, through whatever handler the application chose. Where should the rule "never log the number" live?
hint: Which piece of code is present in every application that logs the struct?

choices.text: In each application's `ReplaceAttr`
choices.why: That depends on every application remembering, and some will not.

choices.text: In a `LogValue` method on the struct
choices.why: Right. The type says once how it is logged, under any handler.

choices.text: In a code review checklist
choices.why: A checklist is a habit; `LogValue` is a guarantee in the type.

choices.text: In the log storage, by deleting matching lines
choices.why: By then the number has already been copied somewhere with weaker protection.

prompt: How did `slog.Group("address", "city", "Recife", "zip", "50000-000")` appear in the JSON?

choices.text: As two keys, `address.city` and `address.zip`
choices.why: That dotted form is what the text handler writes; JSON nests.

choices.text: As one string, `Recife 50000-000`
choices.why: The values kept their own keys.

choices.text: As an object inside the record's object
choices.why: Right: `"address":{"city":"Recife","zip":"50000-000"}`.

choices.text: It was dropped as personal data
choices.why: Nothing in `slog` judges data; it was written.

prompt: With what exit status did `go vet ./attrs` end, after reporting the call missing a final value?
hint: The last line of that transcript.

prompt: What makes a `slog.LevelVar` different from a fixed `Level` in the handler options?
hint: When does the handler read it?

choices.text: It holds several levels at once
choices.why: It holds one level, which can change.

choices.text: It applies only to `Debug` calls
choices.why: It is the minimum level for every call.

choices.text: It changes at run time
choices.why: Right. The handler reads it on every record, so `level.Set` took effect at once.

choices.text: It is stored in the context
choices.why: It is a variable the handler points at; the context carried the request id.

prompt: In `levels/main.go`, why did `log.Info("no context, no request id")` get no `request_id`?
hint: What context reaches the handler from a call without one?

choices.text: It reached the handler with an empty context
choices.why: Right. Only the `…Context` calls carried the id along.

choices.text: `withRequest` skips records at `INFO`
choices.why: `InfoContext` at `INFO` got the id.

choices.text: The level was set to `DEBUG` just before
choices.why: The level decides whether a record is written, not what it carries.

choices.text: Request ids are added only once per program
choices.why: Two records got the same id; nothing counts them.

prompt: Why does the lesson put only the request id in the context, rather than a whole logger?
hint: Where is the decision about how to write records kept?

choices.text: A logger is too large to fit in a context
choices.why: A context can hold any value; size is not the argument.

choices.text: Contexts may hold only strings
choices.why: `WithValue` takes any value.

choices.text: A logger in a context leaks a goroutine
choices.why: No goroutine is involved.

choices.text: The handler stays put
choices.why: Right. Functions log with `InfoContext` and know nothing about ids.

prompt: An operator turns `DEBUG` on in production to investigate an incident. What cost does the lesson name?
hint: What happens to every record that is written?

choices.text: The program has to be restarted
choices.why: With a `LevelVar` nothing restarts.

choices.text: Volume, a hundred times more
choices.why: Right. So it is turned on for as long as needed and set back.

choices.text: Debug records lose their attributes
choices.why: They carry attributes like any other.

choices.text: Errors stop being logged
choices.why: Lowering the level adds records; it removes none.

prompt: Put in order what happens to `log.InfoContext(ctx, "order placed", "order", 1042)` in `levels/main.go`.
hint: The level is checked before anything is built.
items: the level `INFO` is compared with the `LevelVar`
a record is made with the message and `order`
the text handler writes the line

prompt: Match each need with the piece of `slog` that answers it.
hint: Four pieces, four needs, one spare.

pairs.left: the same id on every line about a request
a credential that must never be written

prompt: Which of these calls does `go vet` report? Choose all that apply.
hint: It checks that the arguments after the message come in pairs.

choices.text: `slog.Info("saved", "id")`
choices.why: Yes: a key with no value.

choices.text: `slog.Info("saved", "id", 7)`
choices.why: A key and its value: nothing to report.

choices.text: `slog.Info("saved", slog.Int("id", 7))`
choices.why: A typed attribute stands alone and needs no partner.

choices.text: `slog.Warn("slow", "took_ms", 812, "query")`
choices.why: Yes: the last key has no value.
